# European shares join global sell-off as AI fears mount

Richard Connor | Srinivas Mazumdaru with AFP, Reuters

November 6, 2026

European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets. [...] US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.

The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending plans and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.

By Mithil Aggarwal

HONG KONG — An intensifying rout of tech stocks hit global markets Friday, with a surge of red tickers spreading from Wall Street to Asia and Europe after the blue wave of the U.S. midterm elections fueled fears over AI development.

The steep losses in Asia — Japan’s Nikkei suffered its worst week since 2020 — came after a dramatic plunge in U.S. tech stocks following the success of anti-AIcandidates, which deepened concerns about the durability of the AI boom. # Global market rout deepens after midterms intensify AI fears

Tech stocks plunged in Asia and Europe on Friday after a dramatic selloff in the U.S. following the success of anti-AI candidates.

By Mithil Aggarwal [...] Some $2.3 billion in market value was wiped off the tech-focused Nasdaq 100, which dropped 6.3% on Thursday. Another $2.8 trillion was erased from the S&P 500’s market value as it fell 4.4% — their worst day in 18 months, when President Donald Trump’s global tariffs rocked markets.

U.S. futures were mixed early Friday, but European shares also opened lower after the dramatic selloff continued in Asia.

European shares fell 0.36% on Friday as a global tech selloff erased billions in market value, closing October on a sour note. Despite the session decline, the pan-European STOXX 600 index wrapped up its best monthly performance since June. The pullback followed weak signals from the United States, where tech earnings reignited worries over the heavy capital expenditure required for artificial intelligence.
